identity.title: Does Reinforcement Learning Really Incentivize Reasoning Capacity in LLMs Beyond the Base Model?

problem.claim: The study probes whether RLVR-trained LLMs develop reasoning abilities beyond their base models across model families, algorithms, and math, coding, and visual-reasoning benchmarks using pass@k at large k.

gap.claim: The authors challenge the prevailing belief that RLVR enables continuous self-improvement and novel reasoning abilities exceeding the base model.

contributions.claim: A systematic boundary analysis of current RLVR-trained LLMs using large-k pass@k across diverse settings.
Evidence that current RLVR improves sampling efficiency but does not elicit fundamentally new reasoning patterns and may narrow capability boundaries.
A contrast between RLVR and distillation: distillation is reported to introduce teacher-derived reasoning patterns and expand capabilities.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present a critical, quantitative analysis treating the base model as an upper bound and comparing six RLVR algorithms with distillation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Authors report that RLVR-trained models outperform base models at small k, such as k=1, whereas base models achieve higher pass@k at large k.
Authors report that coverage and perplexity analyses indicate RLVR-generated reasoning paths are already present in the base model’s sampling distribution.
Authors report that six popular RLVR algorithms perform similarly and remain far from optimal in exploiting the base model’s potential.

narrative_sequence.summary: RLVR has improved reasoning performance, motivating the belief that it teaches novel strategies beyond the base model.
The study probes capability boundaries across models, algorithms, and reasoning benchmarks with large-k pass@k.
RLVR improves correct-path sampling efficiency, but large-k comparisons, narrowing boundaries, and distribution analyses point to bounded rather than fundamentally new abilities.
Distillation is reported to expand reasoning patterns, while current RLVR methods leave substantial potential unrealized and motivate new RL paradigms.

source_observation.claim: The abstract contrasts small-k gains with large-k pass@k reversals and uses coverage/perplexity analysis to examine whether reasoning paths are new.

lessons.interpretation: Evaluating only first-sample performance can obscure whether training expands the reachable reasoning distribution or merely changes sampling probabilities.
lessons.application: Pair low-k efficiency metrics with large-k coverage or distributional analyses when claiming that training creates new capabilities.
lessons.exception: This pairing may be unsuitable when compute constraints or the deployment objective specifically concern only low-k inference.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the model families, six RLVR algorithms, benchmarks, or exact large-k values.
It does not provide quantitative effect sizes, training details, or statistical uncertainty.
The distillation setup and the operational definition of a reasoning capability boundary are unspecified.
